content: Lansoprazole is a medication prescribed to treat ulcers, gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), and conditions where the stomach produces excessive acid, such as Zollinger-Ellison syndrome. GERD is a condition where stomach acid flows backward into the esophagus, causing heartburn and potential damage to the esophageal lining. Lansoprazole is also used in combination with other medications to eradicate Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori), a bacterium responsible for causing ulcers. This medication belongs to a class of drugs known as proton-pump inhibitors, which work by reducing the amount of acid produced in the stomach. Lansoprazole is available as a delayed-release capsule and as granules to prepare a delayed-release liquid solution for oral administration. It is typically taken once daily before eating. When used in combination therapy to eliminate H. pylori, it is taken either twice daily (every 12 hours) or three times daily (every 8 hours) for a duration of 10 to 14 days. To ensure consistent use, it is recommended to take lansoprazole at the same time each day. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take lansoprazole exactly as directed, without altering the dose or frequency unless instructed by your doctor. The capsule should be swallowed whole. If swallowing capsules is difficult, the capsule can be opened, and the granules can be sprinkled on one tablespoon of applesauce, Ensure pudding, cottage cheese, yogurt, or strained pears. This mixture should be swallowed immediately without chewing or crushing the granules. Alternatively, the granules can be mixed with 2 ounces of orange juice or tomato juice, stirred briefly, and swallowed immediately. The glass should then be rinsed with additional juice, which should also be consumed immediately. For patients with a nasogastric tube, the capsule can be opened, and the granules mixed with 40 mL of apple juice. This mixture should be injected through the nasogastric tube into the stomach, followed by flushing the tube with additional apple juice. To use the oral solution, empty the contents of a packet into a container with 2 tablespoons of water, stir well, and drink immediately. If granules remain, add more water, stir, and drink immediately. Do not use any liquids or foods other than water, and do not crush or chew the granules. Continue taking lansoprazole even if you feel well, and do not stop taking it without consulting your doctor. This medication may also be prescribed for other uses. Consult your doctor or pharmacist for more information. Before taking lansoprazole, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to lansoprazole or any other medications. Provide a list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, nutritional supplements, and herbal products you are taking. Be sure to mention medications such as ampicillin, digoxin, ketoconazole, theophylline, and iron-containing vitamins. Your doctor may need to adjust your medication doses or monitor you for side effects. If you are taking sucralfate, take it at least 30 minutes after lansoprazole. Inform your doctor if you have or have ever had liver or kidney disease. Additionally, let your doctor know if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. If you become pregnant while taking lansoprazole, contact your doctor. Unless otherwise directed by your doctor, you may continue your normal diet while taking this medication. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to make up for a missed one. Lansoprazole may cause side effects. Notify your doctor if you experience severe or persistent stomach pain or diarrhea. If you experience any unusual problems while taking this medication, contact your doctor. Store lansoprazole in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture (not in the bathroom). Dispose of any outdated or no longer needed medication properly. Consult your pharmacist for guidance on proper disposal. In case of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual collapses or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all appointments with your doctor while taking this medication. Do not share your medication with others. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist.
